response: Routine laboratory markers, such as MCV and AST/ALT ratios, are not useful in differentiating nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) from alcoholic steatohepatitis (ASH). However, these biomarkers may be helpful in guiding the selection of patients for liver biopsy and in targeting therapy, as higher values can reflect the severity of underlying liver disease. Therefore, while they may not be effective in distinguishing between NASH and ASH, they can still play a role in the overall management and treatment of patients with steatohepatitis.
